A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NOVA work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. Neither contains appendix pages. V2 nevertheless references absent appendix sensitivity results, implementation details and visual comparisons, including unresolved '??' references, limiting assessment of that material.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation-quality and inference-efficiency experiments, token-selection and dual-linkage ablations, and entropy analyses in Sections 3–4.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds activation and caching ablations, runtime measurements, and class-conditional ImageNet experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same adaptive activation rule, scale/layer reduction functions, entropy-based token selection and residual-cache procedure, including Equations 1–16. Additional explanations and evaluations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds class-conditional ImageNet generation in Table 9, extending evaluation beyond the text-conditioned generation studied in v1. The original GenEval, DPG-Bench, MJHQ-30K and human-preference evaluations remain.

E2.justification: The existing FastVAR, SparseVAR and SkipVAR benchmark comparator sets are unchanged. New component comparisons introduce fixed-activation NOVA controls in Table 5 and NOVA variants using FastVAR's static token caching in Table 7.

E3.justification: V2 substantially extends the evaluation design with fixed activation scales 6–10, static-cache scales 6–8 with adjusted t_est, and component-level runtime profiling. Its new ImageNet protocol uses VAR-d30/d36 at 256/512 resolution, batch size 5, and FID/IS. These are added protocols; the existing text-to-image settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds dedicated tests of adaptive activation and residual-cache reuse, plus an entropy-overhead breakdown (Tables 5, 7 and 8). These substantially extend component validation beyond v1's entropy-selection and dual-linkage ablations, which remain. The additional claimed hyperparameter sensitivity analysis cannot be inspected because its referenced appendix is absent.

E5.justification: Both versions report four differently seeded images per rewritten prompt for Figure 4 and retain the same entropy mean/range presentation. V2 introduces no new reported run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Existing table values are retained, including v1 Table 5 as v2 Table 6. New results include adaptive activation at 2.89× speedup and 0.72 GenEval versus fixed-scale-7 activation at 2.85× and 0.66; entropy computation taking 1.7 ms, or 0.9% of the profiled scale; and VAR-d36 latency decreasing from 2.89s to 1.97s with FID increasing from 2.63 to 2.79. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1's corresponding scores.

T1.justification: V2 adds a short computational-complexity argument contrasting O(N_t|V|) entropy computation with O(N_t^2 d) self-attention in Section 4.3. The original entropy inequalities, factorization assumptions and method derivations remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contribution: training-free VAR acceleration through entropy-guided adaptive activation, dual-linkage reduction and residual reuse. The new experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations that dynamic caching mitigates error accumulation and that entropy overhead is amortized by computation savings. It also qualifies applicability by attributing the smaller VAR-d30 speed benefit to lower computational redundancy. Earlier interpretations of entropy selection and category-dependent activation remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability statement and repository hyperlink, describes limited benchmark-specific tuning, and explains computation from existing predictive distributions. The original default hyperparameters and hardware remain unchanged. Further implementation details promised in the appendix are unavailable, and adjusted cache-ablation t_est values are unspecified.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a brief connection to label-distribution and federated learning, with six associated references, and adds Kou et al. (2026a) to the token-reduction discussion. The main research positioning remains unchanged. FreqExit's bibliographic update refers to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized terminology and grammar edits, adds analysis paragraphs and acknowledgements, and updates affiliation and conference text. The overall section order and narrative remain intact. New appendix pointers contain unresolved references.

P2.justification: New Tables 5, 7, 8 and 9 substantially expand the experimental displays with activation, caching, runtime and ImageNet comparisons. The former Table 5 becomes Table 6; Table 4 and Figure 8 are relocated, and existing tables receive formatting adjustments. Figures 1–8 retain their content.

improvement.justification: V2 provides direct evidence for previously unisolated activation and caching components, measures entropy overhead, and tests class-conditional generalization. These strengthen support for the unchanged method, while the code link improves access information. The net gain is limited by absent promised appendices, unresolved references and incompletely specified cache controls, which prevent verification of some added robustness and reproducibility claims.
